items.briefing:
Email fraud is on the rise, with attackers increasingly using trusted or compromised credentials to make scam emails appear legitimate — meaning standard warning signs like suspicious sender addresses may no longer be reliable. This makes it harder for staff to spot fraudulent emails, particularly those requesting payments, credential updates, or urgent action.

Be extra cautious with any unexpected email — even from a known contact — that asks you to click a link, transfer funds, or share login details. When in doubt, verify the request by calling the sender directly using a number you already have on file.

featured.title: Attackers exploit trusted credentials in email fraud surge
featured.quote: Email fraud now dominates incidents; attackers bypass multi-factor authentication affecting most Australians.
